elements.evidence: "no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer"
"no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer"

elements.element: Termination fees not characterised/deemed as liquidated damages
elements.evidence: "the Termination for Convenience Fee and the Termination for Cause Fee are not liquidated damages or a penalty"

elements.element: Early-termination fee expressly capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No cap language appears; clause instead states "no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer"

elements.element: That capped fee is the sole liquidated amount
elements.evidence: No 'sole liquidated amount' or equivalent exclusivity language in the redline

reasons: The single replacement operation reverses the deeming language and adds an express statement that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer, which completes both atomic elements of the preferred position at the locked target level.

The fallback (3-month capped early-termination fee as sole liquidated amount) is not satisfied, but that is irrelevant since the drafter is locked to preferred and preferred is fully met; no pieces of the two levels are mixed.

Minimality holds: only the operative second sentence was rewritten, which is the minimum needed both to strip the liquidated-damages characterisation and to state the preferred prohibition; the fallback offer is confined to the non-operative margin comment.

Intent preserved: the underlying Termination for Convenience Fee and Termination for Cause Fee obligations located elsewhere remain effective as contractual fees; only their legal characterisation changes. Note for the record that the retained first sentence (acknowledgement of material adverse impact and damages not susceptible of precise determination) is now largely purposeless recital-style language and could be deleted for tidiness, but it introduces no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic.
